newsitem.title: USA: Boeing must drop exclusive sales - EU's Van Miert.
newsitem.headline: Boeing must drop exclusive sales - EU's Van Miert.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said Friday the European Union will not authorize a merger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp if Boeing continues exclusive provider relationships with Delta Air Lines Inc and AMR Corp's American Airlines.
He said other conditions would also have to be met for the European Union to approve the merger.
"I can't see how possibly we can give our authorization to the merger with such a system in place," he said.
"To our mind this is something which should be declared illegal. And I have no doubt that, if needed, we are going to do so in the European Union," he said.

But he added that the ending of exclusive sales agreements would not be enough, in itself, to win EU approval. "Now, it would not be good enough to bless the merger, that must be clear as well," he said.
Van Miert said he had informed U.S. Federal Trade Commission Chairman Robert Pitofsky of the EU view during a meeting earlier in the day.
"I informed Chairman Pitofsky about the way we are looking upon it," he said.
The FTC is examining the merger in the United States and it is unclear when it will decide what action, if any, to take. If the FTC decides against the merger, it must go to court and challenge it.
Van Miert said that the EU is continuing an in-depth investigation of the merger.
Van Miert said the EU has already communicated its concerns to Boeing and that by May it will finish its investigation.
Then the EU will conduct a private hearing with Boeing, discussing possible remedies to any difficulties it discovers about the merger. A final ruling will be made by the end of July, he said.
Because Boeing sells planes in Europe, EU authority would be required for the merger to go ahead. The EU has never disapproved such large American merger in the past.
